subject: economics
title: Monopsony and Trade Unions
welcome_lead: When power is unequal, classic supply-and-demand breaks down.
meta_desc: A-Level Labour Markets: monopsony, trade unions, wage setting.
final_note: Monopsony and unions can both move outcomes away from competitive equilibrium.

concepts.def: Negotiating pay and terms on behalf of members.
Party with power to set rather than take the wage.
Withdrawal of labour to press demands.
Monopsony employer faces a union - outcome depends on bargaining.

walkthroughs.body_html: A monopsonist faces an upward-sloping labour supply curve. Hiring one more worker raises the wage for all - so marginal cost of labour exceeds the wage. Result: lower wages and employment than competition.
Trade unions raise wages above competitive levels through collective bargaining. If labour demand is elastic, employment falls - but in monopsony, unions can raise both wages and employment.
When a monopsony meets a strong union, outcomes depend on relative bargaining power - strike funds, alternative options, public opinion all matter.

mcqs.q: In a competitive labour market, a union typically:
options: Raises wages and may reduce employment
